parsed_answer.content: Designing a high-throughput, low-latency News Feed and Timeline service in a Core Java environment requires a mastery of concurrent data structures, memory-efficient caching hierarchies, and specialized fan-out strategies. A news feed aggregates content from followed entities (fan-out-on-write or push architecture), whereas a timeline typically focuses on a user's own generated posts (fan-out-on-read or pull architecture). In a production Java backend, handling millions of concurrent timeline requests without violating garbage collection (GC) latency SLAs demands careful allocation tracking, lock-free ring buffers, and optimized priority queues. We must leverage non-blocking concurrency primitives like ConcurrentSkipListMap or custom off-heap memory mapping via Unsafe or Foreign Function & Memory APIs to avoid JVM heap exhaustion during massive fan-out storms.

items: Hybrid Fan-out Strategy: Push updates to active users with small follower counts while pulling on-demand for celebrity accounts with millions of followers to prevent cascading write amplification.
Concurrent Priority Merging: Using a custom Min-Heap or Tournament Tree backed by custom comparators to merge timestamp-ordered streams from multiple followed partition logs in O(K log M) time.

Off-Heap Ring Buffers: Utilizing LMAX Disruptor patterns within the JVM to pass feed mutation events between network ingress handlers and fan-out worker threads without incurring lock contention or object allocation overhead.

parsed_answer.content: Production Gotcha: Never store unbounded user feeds in standard java.util.ArrayList inside a Singleton cache bean. During high-volume timeline pagination, this causes massive object promotion to the old generation, triggering Stop-The-World (STW) Garbage Collection pauses. Instead, use bounded circular buffers, primitive arrays, or Redis sorted sets (ZSET) partitioned by user ID.
